label: New babysitter

what_happens.title: What happens with a babysitter
goals: The steps: the babysitter arrives, a hello time together, goodbye, play, dinner, bedtime, the grown-up comes back
The grown-up always comes back, at the time they say
The house rules and routine stay the same
what_happens.parentSkill: Say exactly when you leave and when you come back, in terms of the routine: "after dinner and pyjamas".

who_is_there.title: Who is my babysitter
goals: The babysitter's name, what they look like, what they like to play
Their job is to keep the child safe and have fun
The grown-up chose them and trusts them
who_is_there.parentSkill: Show a photo of the babysitter and say their name and one fun fact about them.

what_i_do.title: What I do with the babysitter
goals: Show the babysitter my toys, my room and my favourite game
Tell the babysitter what I need
Do my usual bedtime steps with the babysitter
what_i_do.parentSkill: Let your child give the babysitter a "tour" and teach them one game.

if_scared.title: If I miss my grown-up
goals: Goodbye can feel hard, and tears are okay
The worry usually gets smaller after a few minutes of play
Calm tools: a short goodbye ritual, a heart on the hand, a photo, slow breaths
if_scared.parentSkill: Keep goodbyes short, warm and the same every time; never sneak out.

rehearsal.title: Let's practise the babysitter night
goals: Play babysitter with toys: hello, goodbye, play, come back
Say the steps once more, ending with the grown-up coming back
rehearsal.parentSkill: Practise your goodbye ritual with a toy, including the coming back part.

steps: The babysitter rings the bell and says hello
We all play together for a little while
[[GROWNUP]] says goodbye with our goodbye ritual
Play and have dinner with the babysitter
Bath, pyjamas and a bedtime story
[[GROWNUP]] comes back, and I see them when I wake up
sensory: a new voice in the house
a different way of reading the story
a quiet house after the door closes
my own room, my own bed, my own blanket
honestyNotes: Never sneak out to avoid tears; say goodbye honestly. Do not promise the child will not cry or miss you. Give the real return time in routine words and keep it. Make sure the babysitter knows the routine, comfort items and how to reach you.

fallbackAnswer: If you are asleep, [[GROWNUP]] will be there when you wake up.
A babysitter is a grown-up who looks after kids while their grown-ups are out.
Missing someone you love is normal.
You can hug your toy, look at the heart on your hand, and tell the babysitter.
Yes. The house rules and bedtime are the same.
[[GROWNUP]] tells the babysitter all your bedtime steps.
You can show the babysitter your favourite game.
Crying is okay. The babysitter knows how to help.
Lots of kids cry at goodbye and then feel better while they play.
The babysitter does your bedtime steps, just like at home.
First bath, then pyjamas, then a story.
Sometimes worry feels like butterflies in the tummy.
A slow breath and a hug can help the butterflies settle.

techniques.label: A short goodbye ritual
techniques.how: Use the same short goodbye every time: a hug, a kiss and a phrase like "see you after sleep".

techniques.label: A heart on the hand
techniques.how: Draw a small heart on both your hands; press it when missing each other.

techniques.label: Meeting the babysitter first
techniques.how: Invite the babysitter to play once while you are home before the first night alone.

techniques.label: A tour by the child
techniques.how: Let your child show the babysitter the toys, room and favourite game.

techniques.label: A routine card
techniques.how: Write or draw the evening routine for the babysitter so the steps stay the same.

techniques.label: A comfort toy
techniques.how: Keep the comfort toy ready for goodbye time and bedtime.

techniques.label: A photo of the grown-up
techniques.how: Leave a photo of you by the bed or in a pocket.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

ritual: Hello to the babysitter and play together
Our goodbye: hug, kiss, see you after sleep

pain: Goodbyes can feel sore inside. That makes sense.
Let's have one big hug before I go.
separation: I always come back. I'll be here when you wake up.
Press the heart on your hand when you miss me.
unknown: First hello, then goodbye, then play, dinner, story, bed.

strangers: The babysitter is called by name. I chose them, and I trust them.

sensory: The house is the same, and your room and blanket are the same.
The babysitter may read the story in a different voice.

social: You can teach the babysitter your favourite game.

love: I love you while I'm out and when I'm home.
